text.p: -- J.P. Morgan analyst Michael Grant said in a research note that he lowered his rating on Rubbermaid Inc to market performer from buy.
-- He also cut the 1996 earnings estimate to $1.17 per share from $1.37 and the 1997 estimate to $1.40 per share from $1.72.
-- In early New York Stock Exchange trade, Rubbermaid shares shed 1/4 to 22-5/8, just short of the 22-1/8 year low.

-- Grant cited the lower earnings expectations for the downgrade, specifically based on greater competition in juvenile products and lower confidence in the company's ability to pass on higher material costs via price increases; plastic resin prices are up 50 percent from the start of the year.
-- The Little Tikes unit is running into additional new competition from Fischer-Price and is showing weak trends in larger-ticket outdoor items, Grant said.
-- Also, yesterday's announcement of the acquisition of closely-held Graco Children's Products for $320 million is viewed by Grant as a "modest positive."
